saints.name: St. Isidore the Farmer
saints.title: Layman
saints.shortBlurb: A day-laborer of Madrid who sanctified the plough and the field with unceasing prayer…
biography: Isidore was born about 1070 at Madrid to poor parents, who named him for St. Isidore of Seville. He passed his whole life as a hired labourer on the farm of the landowner Juan de Vargas, who came to make him bailiff of his estate, and tradition tells of angels guiding his plough while he was at Mass.

With his wife, María Torribia — venerated in Spain as María de la Cabeza — he shared his bread with the poor; their only son died young. Isidore died on 15 May 1130, and when his body was exhumed in 1212 it was found incorrupt, whereupon his tomb drew pilgrims and cures.

Beatified by Paul V in 1619, he was canonized by Gregory XV on 12 March 1622 in the same ceremony as Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier, Teresa of Ávila, and Philip Neri. A farmworker who never left his fields, he is patron of Madrid and of farmers; in 1947 the National Catholic Rural Life Conference placed the farmers of the United States under his patronage.
saints.knownFor: Sanctity found in the daily labor of the fields.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 15 May
